prompt:
Write a Python module intervals.py in the current folder (standard library only) with three functions.

An interval is a pair (start, end) of ints or floats with start <= end. Input intervals may be given as tuples or two element lists, in any order.

1. merge_intervals(intervals) returns a new list of tuples, sorted by start, where every group of overlapping intervals is combined into one. Intervals that only touch (one ends exactly where the next starts, like (1, 2) and (2, 3)) are also combined into one, giving (1, 3). An empty input returns []. A zero length interval such as (3, 3) is a valid interval and is kept unless it lies inside another one. If any interval has start greater than end, raise ValueError. Do not modify the list that was passed in. Always return tuples, even when the input used lists.

2. total_length(intervals) returns the total length covered by the union of the intervals, so overlapping parts are counted once. total_length([]) is 0.

3. gaps(intervals, lo, hi) returns the list of tuples describing the parts of the range [lo, hi] that are NOT covered by any interval, sorted by start. Intervals are clipped to the range first, so intervals that lie partly or completely outside [lo, hi] only count for the part inside it. Gaps of zero length are never returned. With no intervals the result is [(lo, hi)]. If lo > hi raise ValueError. If lo == hi return [].

Examples:
merge_intervals([(1, 3), (2, 6), (8, 10), (15, 18)]) == [(1, 6), (8, 10), (15, 18)]
total_length([(1, 3), (2, 6), (8, 10)]) == 7
gaps([(2, 4), (6, 8)], 0, 10) == [(0, 2), (4, 6), (8, 10)]
